<ticket source="">
# # Creating a task without a title answers a 500 with a database error

- Ticket: request
- State: open

## Description

# Creating a task without a title answers a 500 with a database error

**Type:** bug / error message

`POST /api/tasks` with `{}` answers `500` and `{"error": "Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 1."}`. With `{"title": ""}` it creates an empty task. A body that is not JSON also answers a 500 with the parser's message. On the page, adding an empty task does nothing visible.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `POST /api/tasks` with a missing, empty or blank (only spaces) `title`, or a `title` that is not a string, answers `400` with `{"error": "title is required"}`, and no task is created.
2. The same rule applies to `PATCH /api/tasks/:id` when the body has a `title`.
3. A title longer than 200 characters (after trimming) answers `400` with `{"error": "title must be at most 200 characters"}`. Titles are saved trimmed.
4. A request body that is not valid JSON answers `400` with `{"error": "invalid JSON body"}`.
5. An unexpected error answers `500` with `{"error": "internal error"}` and never shows the internal message to the client (log it on the server instead).
6. When adding a task fails, the page shows the error message from the API.
7. Tests cover these cases.
</ticket>

plan.summary:
Small bug fix (size S) in a Node/SQLite task tracker: POST /api/tasks with a missing, blank or non-string title currently reaches SQLite and returns a 500 that leaks the database message. {"title": ""} even creates an empty task. A body that is not JSON also returns a 500 with the parser's message. The page does not catch the failed POST, so nothing shows.

The plan is one task, for the `back` role, covering all four files: src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts, public/app.js and test/tasks.test.ts. The client change is a few lines, so a separate front task, or a ux, qa or architect task, would cost more than it saves.

Decisions I made, since the ticket leaves them open:
- Title validation is shared by POST and by PATCH when the body has a `title` key. It checks that the value is a string, trims it, rejects an empty result with "title is required" and rejects more than 200 characters with "title must be at most 200 characters". The trimmed value is what gets saved. A PATCH `title: null` counts as not a string, so it gets a 400. A PATCH without a `title` key leaves the title unchanged.
- A body that parses to something other than a plain object (null, an array, a number) gets 400 "invalid JSON body". This covers the gap the triage security note flagged. An empty body still counts as `{}`.
- Validation runs before the task lookup, so PATCH with a bad title on an unknown id answers 400, not 404.
- The top-level catch answers 500 {"error":"internal error"} and logs the real error with console.error on the server. Validation and JSON errors go through a small typed error with a status, which the catch maps to 400. Nothing else changes.
- On the page, the submit handler catches the API error and calls the existing show(), which fills #error. The form is not reset on failure.

No questions block the work.

A title longer than 200 characters after trimming answers 400 {"error":"title must be at most 200 characters"}; titles are saved trimmed.

tasks.goal: Fix title validation and error handling. (1) src/tasks.ts: add an exported error class (e.g. `HttpError` with `status` and `message`) and an exported `validateTitle(value: unknown): string` that throws HttpError(400,'title is required') when value is not a string or is empty after trim(), throws HttpError(400,'title must be at most 200 characters') when the trimmed length exceeds 200, and returns the trimmed title. createTask(db, title) must call it and save the trimmed value. updateTask must validate the title only when `changes.title !== undefined` (null counts as a non-string, so 400) and save it trimmed; a missing title leaves it unchanged. (2) src/app.ts: readJson must throw HttpError(400,'invalid JSON body') when JSON.parse fails or when the parsed value is not a plain object (null, array, number, string); an empty body stays `{}`. In PATCH, validate the title before looking up the task (400 takes precedence over 404). The catch in createServer must answer the HttpError's status and message when it is an HttpError, and otherwise log the error with console.error on the server and answer 500 {"error":"internal error"}; never send err.message of an unexpected error. Keep the existing 404/405 responses and the `send` helper. (3) public/app.js: in the form submit handler wrap the POST and render in try/catch and call the existing `show(err)` on failure so #error displays the API message; do not call form.reset() on failure; the success path is unchanged (render() already clears #error). (4) test/tasks.test.ts: extend the existing `call` helper style (add a way to send a raw string body with a content-type header for the invalid-JSON cases) and add tests for: POST with {}, {title:''}, {title:'   '}, {title:123}, {title:null} -> 400 'title is required' and the list unchanged; POST with a 201-character title -> 400 'title must be at most 200 characters'; a 200-character title is accepted; ' padded ' is saved as 'padded'; PATCH with an empty, blank, non-string and too-long title -> 400 and the task unchanged; PATCH with only {done:true} still works; invalid JSON ('{nope'), `null` and `[]` bodies on POST and PATCH -> 400 'invalid JSON body'; an unexpected error -> 500 {error:'internal error'} with no internal message (provoke it without changing production code paths, e.g. close the database behind the server or stub it, and silence/assert console.error). Run `npm test` and make it pass. Do not commit.

reviews.summary:
I found nothing that must change, and I report one nit. I read the full diff of the four changed files against the base commit and ran `npm test`: 14 tests pass, 0 fail. I did not run the page in a browser, so the `public/app.js` change is checked by reading only.

What I checked:
- **Acceptance criteria 1–5 and 7 on the server.**
  - `validateTitle` rejects non-string, empty and blank titles with "title is required". It rejects titles over 200 characters after trimming. It returns the trimmed value, which is what gets saved.
  - `createTask` and `updateTask` both use it. In `updateTask`, `null` gives a 400 and a missing title leaves the task unchanged.
  - `readJson` answers 400 "invalid JSON body" for a parse failure and for `null`, arrays, numbers and strings. An empty body is still `{}`.
  - PATCH validates the title before looking up the task, so a bad title on an unknown id gives 400, not 404.
  - The top-level catch answers an `HttpError` with its own status and message. Anything else is logged with `console.error` and answered as 500 `{"error":"internal error"}`, so the SQLite and parser messages no longer reach the client.
  - The 404 and 405 responses and `send` are unchanged.
- **Acceptance criterion 6 (page).** The submit handler wraps the POST, `form.reset()` and `render()` in try/catch and calls `show(err)`. `api()` throws an `Error` carrying the API's message, so `#error` shows it. The form is not reset on failure.
- **Tests.** They go through the real HTTP server and cover each listed case. The 500 test provokes a real SQLite failure by dropping the table from another connection, with no production code change. It asserts the exact response body and that `console.error` was called once. I found no test without value.

What I did not check: browser behaviour, and other clients. Body size limits and `done` validation are out of scope in the ticket.

findings.scenario: PATCH with a title calls tasks.validateTitle in the handler, and updateTask validates the same title again. The result is correct, but the check runs twice. If updateTask were changed later, a reader could be unsure which call enforces the 400-before-404 order.
findings.fix: Keep the early call in app.ts and add a short comment saying it exists so a bad title answers 400 before the 404 lookup. Alternatively, have updateTask validate before its lookup (it already does) and drop the call in app.ts. The order then still holds.

criteria.note: T1 changed the public behaviour; no documentation changed (a task for the docs role would)

report.summary:
Title validation and error handling are fixed. `npm test` passes: 14 tests, 0 failures. I did not run the page in a browser, so the change in public/app.js is untested.

- **src/tasks.ts:** I added an exported `HttpError` class (status plus message) and `validateTitle(value)`. It returns the trimmed title. It throws 400 "title is required" when the value is not a string or is empty after trimming. It throws 400 "title must be at most 200 characters" above 200 characters after trimming. `createTask` validates and saves the trimmed title. `updateTask` validates only when `title !== undefined`, so `null` gives a 400, and a missing title leaves it unchanged.
- **src/app.ts:**
  - `readJson` throws 400 "invalid JSON body" when parsing fails or the body is not a plain object (`null`, array, number, string). An empty body is still `{}`.
  - PATCH validates the title before looking up the task, so a bad title on an unknown id gives 400, not 404.
  - The top-level catch answers an `HttpError` with its own status and message. Anything else is logged with `console.error` and answered as 500 `{"error":"internal error"}`.
  - The 404 and 405 responses and the `send` helper are unchanged.
- **public/app.js:** the submit handler wraps the POST, `form.reset()` and `render()` in try/catch and calls `show(err)` on failure. The form is not reset on failure.
- **test/tasks.test.ts:** new tests for these cases:
  - POST with `{}`, `''`, blank, `123` and `null` titles gives 400, and the list stays the same length.
  - A 201-character title gives 400. A 200-character title is saved, and so is a 200-character title with spaces around it.
  - Titles are saved trimmed on POST and PATCH.
  - PATCH with `''`, blank, `5`, `null` and a 201-character title gives 400 and leaves the task unchanged.
  - PATCH with only `{done:true}` still works and keeps the title.
  - `{nope`, `null`, `[]` and `5` as bodies on POST and PATCH give 400 "invalid JSON body".
  - An unexpected error gives 500 "internal error" with the message hidden and logged. The test uses a file database whose table another connection drops, so no production code path changes.

I did not commit anything.

report.summary:
I confirmed no vulnerabilities in this change. I read the full diff against main (src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts, public/app.js, tests). I did not run the server or the tests myself; this is a read-only review.

What the change does for security:
- A10:2025 (errors that fail open): the top-level catch now sends only `{"error":"internal error"}` for unexpected errors and logs the real error with console.error. The SQLite and parser messages no longer reach the client. Only `HttpError` instances, which are created in the code with fixed messages, have their message sent. It fails closed.
- Input validation: `validateTitle` rejects non-string, empty and blank titles and titles over 200 characters. It runs on POST and on PATCH (before the lookup). `readJson` rejects bad JSON, `null`, arrays and primitives, so `body.title` can no longer throw a TypeError on a null body. A TypeError would have ended as the generic 500.
- Injection: all SQL uses bound parameters. The title is bound only after it is validated to be a string.
- XSS (A05:2025): the page shows the API message and task titles with `textContent`, not `innerHTML`, so a hostile title or error text is not interpreted as HTML.
- A03:2025 (supply chain): the diff does not touch package.json or the lockfile, so there are no new dependencies.

Unconfirmed candidates: none.

Not checked, and out of scope in the ticket: request body size limits (readJson buffers the whole body, so a very large body can use memory); validation of `done` (it is only used as a truthy value, so it has no security effect); the lack of authentication and rate limiting (the app has none by design); a running server or a browser; `npm audit` (no dependency changed).
out_of_scope_findings: src/app.ts readJson buffers the whole request body with no size limit (A06:2025 / availability); the ticket puts body size limits out of scope.
The API has no authentication or rate limiting; out of scope in the ticket.
